meta.title: TFM-BIC — Learn a language one word at a time
meta.description: Lessons, sounds, vocabulary and practice that take a word from unfamiliar to usable. Polish A1 is open now.

hero.title: From a word you can’t read to a word you can use.
hero.lead: Lessons, sounds, vocabulary and practice follow one path: notice a word, hear it, understand it, use it.

word.source: Example from Polish A1 — “A first look at Polish spelling and sounds”

understand.title: A word is more than its spelling.
understand.lead: Every word you meet comes with the pieces that make it usable.

facets.detail: szko·ła — two syllables, stress on the first
sz sounds like English sh, and ł like English w. Roughly: SHKO-wa.
It appears in the A1 page on spelling and sounds.

listen.title: Hear it before you say it.
listen.lead: Vocabulary entries have a Listen control: play a word at normal speed, then slowly, as often as you need.
listen.figureLabel: A sound wave with one rise for each syllable of szkoła

watch.title: Then see how it works.
watch.lead: Short explainer videos are generated from the same lesson content.
watch.status: The first video is in preview: its storyboard is written, and playback is not available yet.

practise.title: Now it’s your turn.
practise.lead: Exercises ask you to choose an answer, decide true or false, or type it. You see straight away why an answer is right.
practise.note: Try it — this example is not saved anywhere.
practise.prompt: Which Polish word means “sorry” or “excuse me”?
practise.explanation: Przepraszam means sorry and excuse me. Dziękuję means thank you, Proszę means please, and Tak means yes.

remember.title: Words come back until they stay.
remember.lead: Save words to My Vocabulary and move them from saved to learning to learned. Each one keeps its meaning and its sound close by.

progress.lead: Lessons move from not started to in progress to completed. Correct exercises and finished lessons earn points, and milestones unlock achievements.
